ny_right_end.blurb: Right End is the east-side stretch of the Starbuck Right cliff, a small forest crag at the foot of Starbuck Mountain in the Indian Lake part of the Adirondacks. Ten traditional lines make up the section, running from 5.8 into the 5.10 range, with a handful of 5.8s and 5.10s and a couple in the middle. Vertical cracks and seams split the face, and this end holds the longest pitches on the whole cliff. Several of its lines are popular among locals, though the lower bands can be mossy or damp, so a brush is a sensible thing to carry.

ny_belleview_slab.blurb: Belleview Slab is a compact slab on Crane Mountain in the southern Adirondacks, sitting around 2,400 feet and about 110 feet tall at its highest. Ten climbs are recorded, nearly all trad with a single sport line, and the grades start near 5.3 and reach into the low 5.10s, so beginners and mid-grade leaders both have options. A left-facing corner crack is the best-known line. Like much of Crane Mountain, the walk in is long and the base can be brushy, and the neighbouring Measles Walls are passed on the way up.

ny_wild_pines.blurb: Wild Pines is a small area in the Lake George region of the Adirondacks, close to Deer Leap Mountain and low down at roughly 860 feet. It mixes bouldering with a few bolted lines: seven boulder problems from V1 up to V7, and three sport routes in the 5.11 to 5.13 range. The boulders are reported as solid, fairly dry in autumn and rarely busy. The cliff carries some unfinished projects, so stick to the lines you know about.

ny_gravity_rules_area.blurb: Gravity Rules Area is a section of Antlion Cliff, a backcountry band of rock in the Gunks south of Millbrook. It begins at the top of the stone steps and carries on leftward. Ten trad routes are stored here, spanning the mid 5.x grades up to the 5.12 range, with a cluster around 5.10. Trees give the wall partial shade. The cliff is still being cleaned, and lower Millbrook-style rock can be sandy and loose, so place gear carefully. Expect a hike of a bit over a mile with a steady climb to reach the cliff.

ny_notch_mountain.blurb: Notch Mountain is an unofficial name for a peak above Wilmington Notch in the Adirondacks, home to low-angle slab climbing that suits beginners. Ten trad routes are recorded, mostly easy: roughly 5.2 to 5.6, with one at the 5.7 level. That makes it a handy place to practice leading, placing gear or setting up top-ropes. A steep trail and herd paths from Route 86 lead to the cliffs in about 10 to 15 minutes. A separate summit cliff sits higher up and is normally reached by rappel.

ny_owls_head_mountain.blurb: Owls Head Mountain is a short summit crag above Keene in the Adirondacks, about 2,800 feet up, with sweeping views of the nearby peaks. Ten routes are recorded, seven trad and three top-rope, with most around 5.6 to 5.10 and a single 5.11. The wall is only about 50 feet high, the rock is mostly clean, and its sunny exposure can keep it usable into early winter and spring. Wind funnels past the face, and since hikers also come to the summit, climbers topping out will have an audience.

ny_warwarsing_boulder.blurb: Warwarsing Boulder is a large block beside the entrance road of the Wawarsing lot in the Trapps section of the Gunks. It has ten problems with easy ones as the backbone, a number of V0 and V1 lines, and a few harder ones up to V6. Both the east and west faces are climbed. It works as a rainy-day fallback, a quick session in fading light, or an alternative when the main lot is full. The drawback is traffic noise from the nearby highway.
